trust_decision.summary: Whether a credential header or credential-shaped field may follow a redirect / be dumped in a log is decided by hard-coded, case- and separator-sensitive name matching in HttpExecutor.prepareRedirectUrlOptions and safeStringifyJson, while the Electron runtime only reaches that check at all when the provider forces redirect: 'manual'.

landing_point.why: The advisory names a cross-origin redirect leak of PRIVATE-TOKEN and mixed-case Authorization in builder-util-runtime; this static method is the only place that decides which headers are deleted when a redirect changes origin, and it only looks at the exact lowercase key headers.authorization.

fix_sites.entry_point: HttpExecutor.request()/doApiRequest() and HttpExecutor.doDownload() (public runtime API used by updater providers and electron-publish publishers)
safeStringifyJson() exported public API (index.ts:16) used for debug/error payload logging by providers and publishers
HttpExecutor.request() request-body debug log (debug(json!) at line 90)
HttpExecutor.request() error-path description: browser response body echoed as 'Data:' via plain JSON.stringify
builder-util-runtime package exports (isSensitiveFieldName / hashSensitiveValue added to the public surface)
removePassword() public export (builder-util main is out/util.js) used by exec()/spawn command logging at util.ts:134 and util.ts:213-215

stripSensitiveEnvVars() / filterSensitiveEnv() public exports: child-process env at util.ts:117-119,148 and app-builder-lib callers (bundledTool.ts:20, yarn.ts:55, FpmTarget.ts:282, snapcraftBuilder.ts:371)
exec() error message built from child-process stdout/stderr (ExecError)
GitHubPublisher constructor (publish configuration / GH_TOKEN) throws InvalidConfigurationError
GitlabPublisher constructor (publish configuration / GITLAB_TOKEN) throws InvalidConfigurationError
GitLabProvider.getLatestVersion() -> Provider.httpRequest() (autoUpdater.checkForUpdates) — the fix inserts createRequestOptions() with redirect: 'manual' here

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about HTTP redirects, while removePassword() is CLI-argument log sanitisation in another package that already hashes password/token/secret stems, so a solver can call it an unrelated, pre-existing sanitiser and leave it (and the parallel SENSITIVE_ENV_KEY_RE matcher at util.ts:83) untouched.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-origin redirects must keep the credential header, non-sensitive headers (User-Agent, Accept, Range) must survive a cross-origin redirect, and the documented http->https upgrade on standard ports is explicitly exempt from stripping — a blanket delete-all-headers or strip-on-any-protocol-change fix breaks authenticated same-origin flows and the backward-compatibility rule.

O6_input_shapes: header-name separators: PRIVATE-TOKEN vs PRIVATE_TOKEN, X-Api-Key vs X_API_KEY (normalization strips '-' and '_')
alternate credential header names: private-token, x-api-key, x-auth-token, x-access-token, x-gitlab-token, cookie, x-csrf-token
object field names: substring match (token, password, secret, authorization, credential, apikey, passphrase, auth) and suffix match (key), case- and separator-insensitive
value type: string values become '<sha256> (sha256 hash)', non-string values become '<stripped sensitive data>'
environment-variable keys (stripSensitiveEnvVars / filterSensitiveEnv) and CLI flag stems (-privateToken, -apiKey, --token, /passphrase, pass:, /b ... /c blocks)
redirect URL shapes: same-origin vs cross-origin, protocol-only and port-only changes, http->https on standard ports exempt

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Differential-download redirect handler re-issues the range request with the same request options, so every header (authorization / private-token coming from autoUpdater.requestHeaders) survives the cross-origin redirect and HttpExecutor.prepareRedirectUrlOptions is never called.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It only re-targets blockmap/range downloads rather than API calls; the handler merely updates the URL and calls followRedirect(), so a solver can treat the advisory's API-level stripping as sufficient.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other package (electron-updater/differentialDownloader) and a different file from the landing point; 2 files away

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Multi-range and single-range byte downloads build options from DifferentialDownloader.createRequestOptions() (which spreads options.requestHeaders) and neither inspect 3xx responses nor strip headers, so in Electron the net layer follows the redirect with the credentials attached.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Range requests are treated as pure data fetches, and the comment at multipleRangeDownloader.ts:124 states that Electron handles redirects automatically, so they can be argued outside the redirect-header concern.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the previous route, separate file (and DifferentialDownloader.ts:276-306 for readRemoteBytes)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Provider.httpRequest() for every provider except GitLabProvider (added by the fix) and PrivateGitHubProvider (pre-existing manual redirect) sends no redirect: 'manual', so under ElectronHttpExecutor the net layer follows redirects itself and prepareRedirectUrlOptions never runs for API requests carrying autoUpdater.requestHeaders credentials (set at packages/electron-updater/src/AppUpdater.ts:169 and pushed to the provider at AppUpdater.ts:489).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only GitLab names a credential header inside the provider (PRIVATE-TOKEN); the other providers look unauthenticated, so a solver can argue there is nothing to strip on their requests.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the fix's GitLabProvider but a different base class; 1 file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second redirect handler that calls HttpExecutor.prepareRedirectUrlOptions before re-issuing the range request
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the download path already re-implements redirect handling and reuses the same requestHeaders (which may carry authorization/private-token); a maintainer hardening redirects would naturally patch here next.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a duplicate token->header-name mapper that also produces PRIVATE-TOKEN for publisher uploads
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same mapper already exists twice (updater and publisher); the fix only hashed this publisher's error message, so a sibling redirect-header hardening (or an addSensitiveRedirectHeader call) is realistic here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: SENSITIVE_ENV_KEY_RE as a third independent field-name matcher beside safeStringifyJson's list and removePassword's stems
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: three separate matchers exist at the pinned commit and the fix only partially unifies them, so another redaction helper (e.g. for a YAML config dump) is a plausible maintainer addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: getSafeEffectiveConfig() serialises the whole build configuration through safeStringifyJson and dumps it to YAML
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the effective config is written out and only cscLink is manually hidden today; a maintainer could add isSensitiveFieldName-style filtering here.

O9_family: sensitive data exposure / credential leak (CWE-200): hard-coded credential-name matching at redirect, log and environment sinks

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=14.14, pnpm 11 workspace (packageManager pnpm@11.1.0), tsc --build via 'pnpm compile', eslint, vitest 3
O10_build.project_tests: test/src/httpExecutorTest.ts — existing vitest suite for HttpExecutor.prepareRedirectUrlOptions (same-origin preservation, cross-origin stripping, http->https upgrade); test/src/builder-util/utilTest.ts — removePassword / filterSensitiveEnv suites; run through pnpm ci:test (ts-node test/vitest-scripts/run-vitest.ts)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add PRIVATE-TOKEN (and case-insensitive names) to the delete list inside prepareRedirectUrlOptions, leaving the log/env/CLI/publisher redaction sites and the provider redirect mode untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: packages/app-builder-lib/src/binDownload.ts:47-52 validates env-derived binary-download URLs against '://', '..' and leading '/', a different redirect-related protection that this advisory does not cover; not pursued.
